newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK property surpassed expectations in 96 - surveyor.
newsitem.headline: HK property surpassed expectations in 96 - surveyor.

text.p: Hong Kong's property market far exceeded expectations in 1996, based on a surge in confidence in the territory after its handover in June, property surveyor Jones Lang Wootton (JLW) said on Tuesday.

"Activity over the past 12 months has clearly shown full recovery of Hong Kong's property market. Not only has transactional volume increased, investment perception on the market has also changed," JLW said in a statement.
It said the recovery was the result of various factors, including confidence in the post-handover government and leader-in-waiting Tung Chee-hwa.
Hong Kong becomes a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
JLW said a more favourable economy, expectations of low inflation and an increase in the inflow of funds after the handover had also improved consumer spending.
Capital growth in strata-titled office and luxury residential sales surpassed expectations in 1996, particularly in the last quarter, it said.
"Overall office capital values increased by 29.7 percent in the fourth quarter whilst overall residential capital values rose by 23.4 percent during the same period," it said.
Addressing the perception of an oversupply of office space, JLW said availability of prime space in districts such as Central and Causeway Bay were in fact limited in 1997.
"This could place pressure on rents in the prime areas in the near term," it said.
